text: Good evening ma/sir, please I am so sorry to be disturbing you at this hour, I know you people are busy with plenty serious cases. I am a foster carer and the baby girl staying with us is 3 months old. Since yesterday she started having these small spots that the GP's receptionist said sounds like chickenpox. Two of the older children in the house had it last week so I am not surprised, but she is so tiny and that is what is worrying me. Tonight I checked her temperature and it is 38.5. The spots are itching her, she keeps trying to rub her face on my shoulder and I have cut her nails short so she will not scratch herself. Apart from that she is behaving like herself sha. She is feeding well, taking her bottle normally, smiling at me, and she was even cooing small when I changed her. I just don't want to be the one that waited and something happened, because she is not my own child and I must report everything properly to the social worker. Please is there something I should be doing for the itching, and is the temperature something to worry about at her age? Once again sorry for the trouble, God bless you for the work you are doing.
